content.title: About
content.content: Baked potato with the peel eaten is a popular side dish and standalone meal obtained by roasting whole tubers in the oven until the skin turns golden and crisp. The peel retains most of the nutrients, while baking intensifies flavor and creates a soft interior with a crunchy exterior.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The potato skin contains more fiber, vitamins, and minerals than the flesh.
Baking preserves more antioxidants than boiling.
Around the world baked potatoes are served with a variety of toppings: sour cream, cheese, herbs, or spices.
Potatoes were domesticated in South America over 7,000 years ago and quickly became a staple worldwide.
Eating the skin helps lower the glycemic index of the dish.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: The skin provides both soluble and insoluble fiber, supporting healthy digestion and satiety.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Baked potatoes retain a significant amount of vitamin C, which aids immune function and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance, blood pressure, and muscle function.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: When baked without excessive oil, the dish remains low‑calorie, suitable for weight management.

items.title: Provides vitamin B6
items.content: Vitamin B6 is involved in protein metabolism and neurotransmitter synthesis.

items.title: Solanine content
items.content: If the potato has sprouted or developed green spots, the skin may contain solanine—a toxin that should be removed.

items.title: Potato allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience allergic reactions to potatoes.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Baked potatoes can raise blood sugar quickly; people with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Potential contaminants
items.content: High‑temperature cooking (e.g., on foil or grill) can form acrylamide and other compounds; moderate oven temperatures are preferable.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Baked potatoes with the skin can be enjoyed plain, split and topped with cheese, cottage cheese, herbs, or used in salads and sandwiches. Before baking, potatoes are often brushed with a little olive oil and seasoned with salt, pepper, and herbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store raw tubers in a cool, dark, well‑ventilated place. After baking, let them cool, then keep in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Reheat in the oven to restore the crisp skin.
